reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: A skeletal dysplasia characterised by a distinctive 'fetal face' with frontal bossing, hypertelorism, a short upturned nose and a broad forehead
The autosomal recessive form is caused by ROR2 mutations and is generally more severe; dominant forms arise from WNT5A, DVL1, DVL3 and related genes in the non-canonical WNT pathway
Mesomelic limb shortening (short forearms and lower legs) is typical, with brachydactyly and short stature
Genital hypoplasia is characteristic, with a micropenis in males and clitoral/labial hypoplasia in females, and may cause diagnostic confusion
The recessive ROR2 form frequently includes vertebral segmentation defects with scoliosis and rib anomalies
Dental crowding, gum hypertrophy and a broad mouth are common oral features
Some dominant forms (notably certain DVL and WNT5A variants) are associated with osteosclerosis
Diagnosis is clinical and radiographic, confirmed by molecular testing to distinguish the dominant and recessive forms for counselling
reference.pathophysiology: Robinow syndrome is a disorder of the non-canonical WNT/planar cell polarity signalling pathway, which governs skeletal patterning, limb outgrowth and craniofacial and genital development. The recessive form is caused by loss of function of ROR2, a receptor tyrosine kinase that acts as a co-receptor for WNT5A; the dominant forms result from variants in WNT5A itself or in downstream DVL genes. Disruption of this pathway impairs the coordinated growth and orientation of skeletal elements, producing the mesomelic limb shortening, vertebral anomalies, characteristic facial appearance and genital hypoplasia.
additionalDifferentials: Aarskog-Scott syndrome (FGD1, facial and genital features)
Other mesomelic dysplasias (e.g. Langer, Leri-Weill dyschondrosteosis, SHOX-related)
Disorders of sex development for the genital hypoplasia
additionalInvestigations: Molecular testing of ROR2 and of dominant genes (WNT5A, DVL1, DVL3) to define the form
Skeletal survey to document mesomelic shortening, brachydactyly and vertebral/rib anomalies
Spinal radiographs and follow-up for segmentation defects and scoliosis in the recessive form
Renal and cardiac assessment where associated anomalies are suspected
Endocrine and genital assessment to characterise hypoplasia and guide management
Dental and orthodontic evaluation for crowding and gum overgrowth
redFlags: Progressive scoliosis from vertebral segmentation defects in recessive disease
Congenital cardiac or renal anomalies causing functional compromise
Marked genital hypoplasia requiring endocrine evaluation and psychosocial support
Airway or feeding difficulty in severely affected neonates
reference.prognosis: Intelligence is usually normal and life expectancy is generally good, particularly in the dominant forms; the recessive ROR2 form is more severe, with skeletal and vertebral complications, but with orthopaedic, endocrine and multidisciplinary care most individuals do well.
pitfalls: Misattributing genital hypoplasia to a primary disorder of sex development and missing the syndromic diagnosis
Not distinguishing dominant from recessive forms, leading to incorrect recurrence-risk counselling
Overlooking vertebral segmentation anomalies and progressive scoliosis on follow-up
Confusing the facial features with a fetal alcohol phenotype
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: Orthopaedic management of mesomelic limb shortening, brachydactyly and limb deformity with bracing and corrective surgery as needed
Spinal surveillance and orthopaedic treatment of vertebral segmentation defects, rib anomalies and scoliosis, particularly in the recessive ROR2 form
Endocrine assessment and hormonal treatment of genital hypoplasia, including androgen therapy for micropenis where indicated
Dental and orthodontic management of crowding and gingival overgrowth
Screening for and management of associated renal and cardiac anomalies
Coordinated care through a multidisciplinary skeletal dysplasia team
Genetic counselling distinguishing recessive ROR2 disease from dominant WNT5A/DVL forms, with molecular testing and family screening
